html:
The founder of the Ming dynasty of China, born Zhu Yuanzhang, who ruled from 1368 to 1398. He rose from the very bottom of society to the throne.

His parents and brothers died in a famine in 1344, and he became a novice in a Buddhist monastery, begging to survive. He then joined the Red Turban rebels against the Mongol Yuan dynasty, rose to lead his own army, and took Nanjing in 1356. In 1368 he declared the Ming dynasty and drove the Mongols out of Beijing.

As emperor he worked to rebuild a ruined countryside and to control everything himself:

  • He ordered land surveys and household registers to fix taxes and labour.
  • He issued the Great Ming Code.
  • In 1380 he abolished the post of chief minister and ran the government directly.
  • He banned private sea trade.

He was suspicious and cruel. Purges of officials and their families killed tens of thousands. His capital was Nanjing. His grandson succeeded him but was soon overthrown by his son, the Yongle Emperor, who moved the capital to Beijing.
sum: The founder of the Ming dynasty of China, born Zhu Yuanzhang, who ruled from 1368 to 1398. He rose from the very bottom of society to the throne.
